study_identification.title: Individualized resting-state functional connectivity abnormalities unveil two major depressive disorder subtypes with contrasting abnormal patterns of abnormality

study_characteristics.study_objective: This study aimed to identify major depressive disorder (MDD) subtypes based on subject-level functional connectivity abnormalities using a tolerance interval-based approach. The study also sought to assess the reproducibility and sensitivity of these subtypes and evaluate their utility in improving case-control discriminability.

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: Standard analysis protocols across study sites; Craddock 200 brain atlas

quality_checking_detail.answer: Global signal regression was not applied. Mean frame-wise displacement (mean FD) was used as a covariate.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: ComBat method was applied to harmonize the functional connections across 25 research sites.

response_variable.answer: Pairwise Pearson's correlation coefficients between regional signals (functional connectivity)

predictor_variables.answer: Age; Sex; Study site; Head motion (mean FD)

predictor_effects.answer: Sex, age, study site, and head motion (mean frame-wise displacement, mean FD) were controlled for in the two-sample t-tests for characterizing subtypes.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study used ComBat to harmonize data across sites, addressing site effects. Head motion was included as a covariate in statistical analyses.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: To address this, we applied the Combat method to harmonize the functional connections across these sites. Combat has been shown to effectively remove site-related variance while preserving biological variability in neuroimaging studies [37-39]. ... Functional connectivity abnormalities for each subtype, relative to HCs, were also assessed using two-sample t-tests, controlling for sex, age, study site, and head motion (mean frame-wise displacement, mean FD) [51, 52].

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study performed subsampling validation and leave-one-site-out validation to assess cluster stability.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: Cluster stability was evaluated using 100 randomly selected subsample (90% of patients) and leave-one-site out validation.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study did not use a separate independent dataset from the same domain for validation.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study applied the same analysis pipeline to a dataset of schizophrenia patients from the COBRE dataset to examine the specificity of the findings.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: Finally, to examined whether extreme functional connectivity pro /uniFB01 le we reported is speci /uniFB01 c to MDD, we applied the same analysis pipeline to a dataset of schizophrenia patients from Centre for Biomedical Research Excellence (COBRE, http://fcon_1000.-projects.nitrc.org/indi/retro/cobre.html) [53].

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Linear regression models were used to explore the relationship between extreme functional connections and clinical characteristics. Two-sample t-tests were used to compare subtypes. Linear SVMs were used for classification.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The study identified two robust MDD subtypes with contrasting patterns of functional connectivity abnormalities, which improved case-control discriminability.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Two MDD subtypes were identified. Subtype 1 (N=394) showed increased functional connectivity, while subtype 2 (N=882) showed decreased functional connectivity. These subtypes were stable and reproducible. The subtypes improved case-control classification accuracy (71.66% for subtype 1 vs. HCs, 63.26% for subtype 2 vs. HCs) compared to the overall MDD group (55.10%).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The study was cross-sectional, had limited clinical data, and did not account for confounding factors like smoking and drinking. Patients with comorbidities were excluded.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The tolerance interval method was used to identify subject-level functional connectivity abnormalities, which may be a valuable approach for analyzing heterogeneous clinical populations.
